bug_semantics: ScopedFs is intended to confine a user to a base directory. For an in-scope symlink whose out-of-scope final target does not yet exist, filepath.EvalSymlinks(target) returns fs.ErrNotExist. The vulnerable within()/WithinScope loop then replaces the link path with its lexical parent, resolves that in-scope directory, and returns true. guard() therefore permits OpenFile, while the subsequent base OpenFile with os.O_CREATE|os.O_TRUNC follows the symlink at the OS layer and creates attacker-controlled content outside the scope. An authenticated HTTP user with Create and Modify can reach this through POST /api/resources/<link>?override=true (and equivalent write paths). Existing out-of-scope targets are rejected; the escape is specific to a dangling target. The advisory declares github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/v2 <=2.63.15 affected and 2.63.16 first patched.
flaw_origin: Incomplete symlink-confinement remediation in 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b. That one-parent commit first adds files.WithinScope and the faulty fs.ErrNotExist nearest-existing-ancestor loop to files/file.go, calls it from http/resource.go before OpenFile, and even documents that a dangling symlink is allowed because its containing directory is validated. Its direct parent 0231b7ebdfbe77a6c54027d30c4856c3fd81ee4d has neither WithinScope nor that fallback. Commit 7c2c0a11b31b2bb214d741005a0b02b1764208b3 later moves the same loop into new files/scoped.go as ScopedFs.within and is a carrier/refactor, not the first writer. The BIC first ships in v2.63.6; the residual remains in the predecessor issue's nominally patched v2.63.14 and in v2.63.15. Earlier releases had the broader unguarded symlink behavior, which explains the advisory's inclusive <=2.63.15 range; this BIC identifies the first writer of the residual patch-gap logic audited here.
ai_marker: BIC commit object 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b has human author and committer Henrique Dias <mail@hacdias.com> and the exact canonical trailer 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>'. Verified with git cat-file commit on the BIC itself. No PR text, branch metadata, carrier commit, or fix-commit AI signal was used.
evidence: Reproduce in the assigned clone. (2) `git log -L :WithinScope:files/file.go 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b` identifies 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b as the function's first writer, and `git log -S'for errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist)' --all -- files/file.go files/scoped.go` shows 847d08b introduction, 7c2c0a1 relocation, and 64511ce closure. (3) `git show 0231b7ebdfbe77a6c54027d30c4856c3fd81ee4d:files/file.go` contains no WithinScope, and the parent's http/resource.go writeFile proceeds from MkdirAll directly to afs.OpenFile; `git diff 0231b7ebdfbe77a6c54027d30c4856c3fd81ee4d..847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b -- files/file.go http/resource.go` directly verifies the added faulty lines. (4) `git show 7c2c0a11b31b2bb214d741005a0b02b1764208b3 -- files/file.go files/scoped.go` shows deletion of WithinScope and addition of the same nearest-ancestor loop as ScopedFs.within, so 7c2c0a1 is not the BIC. (5) `git show 64511ce45e3be379e965f7f4fb0929a068d5bb81 -- files/scoped.go files/file_test.go http/resource_test.go` shows the direct fix: Lstat a dangling symlink, Readlink and follow its destination before the scope comparison, plus unit and authenticated POST regression tests which assert no out-of-scope file is created. Its parent is be23ab3a15bf957928ecfed88de5ab67850c1b9c. (6) `git rev-parse v2.63.15^{commit} v2.63.16^{commit}` yields be23ab3a15bf957928ecfed88de5ab67850c1b9c and bd1520fe095d2f373f8fbcbfc01f855ade7e90fb; `git tag --contains 64511ce45e3be379e965f7f4fb0929a068d5bb81 --sort=version:refname` starts at v2.63.16, while `git diff v2.63.15^{commit}..v2.63.16^{commit} -- files/scoped.go files/file_test.go http/resource_test.go` contains the dangling-symlink fix and regressions. `git tag --contains 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b --sort=version:refname` starts at v2.63.6. (7) `git cat-file commit 847d08bdd135e5c3659f2e6dea2f0cd36617af9b` gives parent 0231b7e, author/committer Henrique Dias, and the exact Claude Opus 4.8 Co-Authored-By trailer. The BIC has one parent and three logically separate advisory hunks, but no preserved member-commit topology in the clone; the vulnerable hunk is atomic in this commit object, so no squash member SHA is claimed.
reasoning: The security invariant is that a checked pathname and the pathname dereferenced for a write must resolve to the same in-scope destination. The BIC's fallback checks a different object: after EvalSymlinks reports the dangling final link's missing destination, it discards the link component and validates only the lexical parent. OpenFile later dereferences the discarded link and creates the external target. The exact faulty guard and its explicit best-effort exception first appear in 847d08b; direct-parent inspection confirms those lines are absent, -L/-S history rejects the later 7c2c0a1 move as origin, and 64511ce directly closes the same gap and adds matching regression coverage. Because the BIC commit object itself canonically attributes code to Claude Opus 4.8, AI is causally attributed at the first writer of this incomplete remediation, not merely on a later carrier or fix. Verdict: AI_ROOT_CAUSE.
